exposure: Hospitalization for severe COVID-19 vs. obstetric reasons
outcome: Use of general anesthesia for cesarean delivery
cohort: The study included nearly all births to women with a confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection within six weeks before hospitalization in Belgium, between March 2020 and February 2021.
finding: While overall obstetric interventions like cesarean delivery and induction largely remained at pre-pandemic levels, SARS-CoV-2 infection increased medically induced preterm delivery and the use of general anesthesia for cesarean delivery.
mod_finding: Although the majority of women gave birth vaginally and overall cesarean delivery rates did not significantly increase after adjusting for confounders, the use of general anesthesia for cesarean delivery was more common in the infected group.
